key_findings: **BONUS: Sqwt::InputBindingCollectionInterface::vftable @ 0x00F90F00 identified**. Different class from Sqwt::Input::InputBindingCollection (lives in Sqwt:: namespace, not Sqwt::Input::). This is a SEPARATE interface class.

**+0xB4 writer hypothesis**: the MSVC multiple-inheritance pattern fits the evidence. A concrete derived class (e.g. Sqwt::Window, Sqwt::Controls::ListBox) inheriting BOTH Sqwt::InputElement (primary base at +0x00) AND Sqwt::InputBindingCollectionInterface (secondary base at +0xB4) would have its ctor write the Interface vftable at object+0xB4. This explains why InputElement/RaptureElement/XamlElement ctors don't write +0xB4 (they're primary-base-only) - the +0xB4 writer is the derived-class ctor.
**Closes part of the deferred[1] (+0xB4 hunt) ahead of schedule**: the Interface vftable VA is now known. Next tier will find the derived-class ctors that write it.

**Memory layout consistency check**: Sqwt::InputElement::vftable (0x01069A6C) and Sqwt::Input::CommandBindingCollection::vftable (0x01069B90) are 0x124 bytes apart - emitted in the same data block by the linker, consistent with the InputElement+CommandBindingCollection composition pattern. InputBindingCollection::vftable (0x00FA2ECC) is 0xC6E08 bytes away - emitted as a separate type (because it's used independently in addition to being embedded).
